description: A dedicated-storage plugin whose migration names its objects with the `plugin_<normalizedId>_` prefix MUST have them applied, and the object MUST land under exactly the name the migration wrote. The case asserts the EFFECT via `sm db dump` rather than the success line on stdout: human output is not contract, and the contract here is precisely that the physical name is the authored one, which is what a rewriting kernel would break while still reporting success. This is also the positive control the namespace rows needed, since a kernel that rejected every plugin migration would satisfy the refusal case on its own. The manifest declares the LOGICAL table name while the SQL writes the PHYSICAL one, deliberately: the prefix derives from the plugin id, so restating it in the manifest would only add a second place to get it wrong.
